## v0.30.0rc2

v0.30.0rc2

Pre-release

Compare

### Features

  * Added DeepSeek V4.1 support on Model Runner V2, with AscendStore preparation for V4.1. #16899 #16973
  * Extended Model Runner V2 with fine-grained TP (MLP, embedding, o_proj in graph mode) and async CPP scheduling. #17361 #16967 #17380
  * Added the TurboQuant 4-bit latent KV cache for SFA (GLM-5.2/5.3) and DSA (DeepSeek V4 Flash; A2/A3 only) and extended the packed KV cache to the V1 runner; added DeepSeek V4.1 PCP support, GQA PCP and DCP stacking, and graph execution for sharded decode requests in PCP. #18048 #17992 #18066 #18196
  * Enabled sparse SFA C8 (INT8 packed KV cache) for GLM-5.3-Flash, and supported C8-MXFP (FP8 KV cache with E8M0 scales) and INT8 C8 RoPE0 on A2/A3. #17180 #16706
  * Added KV Pool support for GLM-5.3-Flash non-layerwise pooling and Mamba in Mooncake layerwise, plus layerwise memcache DRAM/SSD pooling. #16945 #17287 #17698
Please follow the official documentation to get started.

### Highlights

  * MiniMax-M3 on Atlas 800 A3 and 950DT Products: Added BF16, W8A8, and ModelOpt-compatible MXFP8 serving paths, with optimized MSA index-score, top-k, FlashDecoding, tensor-parallel communication, and the 950DT Products FP8 sparse-attention path. #14412 #14539 #13142 #13987 #15897 #15926
  * DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 950DT Products: Added the validated DSpark serving path, including DSpark integration with DSA-CP and SparseFlashMla-based BF16 KV sparse attention. Eligible compressor, indexer, sparse-attention, DSpark, and local DSA-CP metadata is built asynchronously on Model Runner V1. #13249 #13506 #13716 #15776
  * Speculative-decoding and serving stability: Hardened sequence-length boundaries, empty-context handling, draft-state publication, rejection sampling, request token validation, and distributed MemCache initialization. #16513 #16720 #17276 #16215 #16161 #17308

### Features

  * Added a ModelOpt-compatible MXFP8 path for MiniMax-M3. With `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, MSA and index caches use native FP8 E4M3 while dense GQA layers use BF16 unless explicitly configured otherwise. #14412 #15897 #15926
  * Added DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark on 950DT Products, including DSA-CP integration and SparseFlashMla-based BF16 KV sparse attention. #13249 #13506 #13716
  * Added DeepSeek-V4-Flash layerwise KV-cache reuse support for physical layers with multiple main cache specifications. #17081
  * Integrated vLLM StartPlan so repeat startups can reuse measured KV-cache budgets and graph-capture results. #15654
  * Integrated the GMM-SiTU operator for supported MoE paths. #15871

### Hardware and Operator Support

Model  | Supported hardware in v0.27.1rc1  | Release scope
--- | --- | ---
MiniMax-M3  | Atlas 800 A3 and 950DT Products  | W8A8 on Atlas 800 A3 and W8A8C8 on 950DT Products; two-node 1P1D serving and KV Cache Pool deployment
DeepSeek-V4-Flash  | 950DT Products  | W4A8C8; two-node 1P1D DSpark serving and KV Cache Pool deployment

  * Integrated the AscendC MSA index-score operator into MiniMax-M3 prefill, decode, and speculative-decode paths. #14539
  * Added the MiniMax-M3 950DT Products FP8 MSA and index top-k path, including the release-branch AscendC FP8 MSA index-score backport. #15897 #15926
  * Added native non-power-of-two MLA head support without Q-head padding or output slicing. #15882
  * Integrated GMM-SiTU for supported MoE paths. #15871

### Performance

Unless stated otherwise, these optimizations are selected automatically for the targeted path and need no additional configuration.

  * Optimized MiniMax-M3 MSA index-score computation for prefill, decode, and speculative decode. #14539
  * Reworked MiniMax-M3 decode score computation and TP communication to exchange index queries and local top-k candidates instead of full index KV data. #13142
  * Reduced the MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention score operator cost and added FlashDecoding support. #13987
  * Overlapped shared-expert input/output collectives and projections with routed-expert computation in the supported MoE multistream path. #15974
  * Built DeepSeek V4 compressor, indexer, sparse-attention, and DSpark metadata asynchronously on eligible Model Runner V1 paths. #15776
  * Improved DeepSeek V4 DSA-CP prefill execution by aligning sequence parallelism with the model and attention collectives. #16021
  * Prefetched two AscendStore layers by default to reduce layerwise KV Pool stalls. This does not affect their availability in the earlier releases and release candidates that include them, where they received extensive functional and performance validation. Users can continue deploying those versions and use them as a base for custom development and model-specific extensions:
    * DeepSeek-R1

  * Enabling `additional_config.enable_dsa_cp` now emits an advance deprecation warning. Starting with v0.29.0, DSA-CP will be deprecated for Model Runner V2 deployments; Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) will provide full coverage and replace it. The Model Runner V1 path will remain available until Model Runner V1 is removed, after which DSA-CP will be removed completely. DSA-CP behavior is unchanged in v0.27.1rc1. #15890

Remove this key before upgrading. Unless stated otherwise, these optimizations are selected automatically for the targeted path and need no additional configuration.

After MRV2 fully supports the agreed SFA model and feature scope, the project will deprecate `enable_dsa_cp`, publish a migration window, and remove the legacy feature and code. ...   * [Input] Complete MRV2 support for SFA models — close graph, speculative decoding, C8, P/D, cache-sharing, accuracy, and performance gaps.
DSA  | Sparse-attention algorithm, index selection, and SFA-specific tensor/kernel contract
DSA-CP  | Legacy SFA execution feature selected by `enable_dsa_cp`; combines DSA-specific token/layout processing with TP/SP communication
PCP  | MRV2 compute-partitioning axis for balanced prefill execution; expands the process world
DCP  | Decode KV-cache sequence-sharding axis; reuses ranks and exclusively owns KV slot/shard layout
MRV2  | Model Runner V2 and its virtual-batch PCP lifecycle

The phrase PCP replaces DSA-CP means product and user capability replacement. It does not mean that PCP absorbs the DSA sparse-attention algorithm or that the two implementations become one class. The DSA-specific kernel and layout adaptations remain SFA backend responsibilities, but their input partition comes from MRV2 PCP rather than from the legacy `enable_dsa_cp` feature.

The mandatory ownership rules are:

  1. PCP owns global-to-rank-local prefill work partitioning and global-order restoration.
  2. The SFA backend owns sparse indexer metadata, SFA Q/KV layout, kernel preparation, and SFA output layout.
